title: Moving fire survivors off FEMA interim housing
summary: As of August 31, Kīlohana's temporary housing units and land are moving from FEMA and HHFDC to the County of Maui, though not every resident will be eligible to stay, and some residents did not know about the transfer. The county is meeting with FEMA so caseworkers can meet residents together. About 1,100 households remain in interim housing, which officials expect to be near zero by 2030.

timeline.text: Maui County announced a Housing Navigator Program to help wildfire-affected households access County-supported interim housing, including Kīlohana, and financial assistance.

source.quote: Eligible households may also receive rental assistance or help exploring County-supported temporary housing options, including Hale ʻO Lāʻie in Kīhei and Kilohana in Lahaina.

timeline.text: The County's Current Awards page lists a $15,000,000 award to BDO Government Services for disaster rental assistance and case management under the Disaster Interim Housing Program.

timeline.text: FEMA temporary housing assistance for Maui wildfire survivors was extended to February 2027, which is context for the clinician's concern about residents being made to leave at month's end.

source.publisher: Office of the Governor, State of Hawaiʻi
source.quote: U.S. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem has approved Hawaiʻi's request to extend FEMA Temporary Housing Assistance for Maui wildfire survivors until February 2027, providing critical stability for individuals and families still recovering from the August 2023 wildfires.
